text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today, continuing a broader downtrend over the past two weeks as oil prices have retreated. Crude dropped notably over the weekend—Saudi Arabia restored pipeline flows through the Red Sea to around 3.5 million barrels per day, easing supply concerns that had been pushing prices higher. US oil is trading at $96.41 per barrel, down from levels that supported the stock's gain earlier in the week.

The stock's 11% decline over two weeks reflects a shift in the oil market's risk backdrop. While Middle Eastern geopolitical tensions remain real—U.S. and Iranian officials are in separate ceasefire talks—the immediate supply squeeze has begun to ease as key export routes come back online, removing a near-term bullish prop for energy stocks.
